turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Please come in, sir. I will check the pressure and pulse before the doctor calls you.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, sister, thank you. We left quite early actually, but the fast train was held up at Matunga, so I was worrying we would miss the token, and still we are only a little late.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sit straight and give her the arm. You were talking the whole way in the auto also.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Kindly keep the arm loose. Blood pressure is 148 over 92. Pulse is eighty-two. Oxygen saturation is 98 percent. Doctor will see you now.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): 148 over 92, is it. At home the small machine shows something around 130, but my son bought that during lockdown and I don't trust it fully anymore.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello, I am Dr. Mehta. Do sit, both of you. Tell me, what brings you in today?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Just a check-up, doctor, nothing dramatic. My wife has been on at me since Diwali that at sixty-three one should not only wait for a problem to come. I am still working, accounts for a small transport firm in Dadar, so I keep postponing these things.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): A check-up is perfectly reasonable. How have you been feeling in yourself, day to day?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Day to day I am alright. I sleep, I take my meals, morning tea and two biscuits, office by train, home by seven. If she has made poha I eat that, otherwise just the tea. I don't feel sick as such.
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, he is leaving out the stairs. At the station he stops halfway now and holds the railing.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): That is only because the staircase is steep, Sheela, and the crowd pushes. It is not a pain. I am not having chest pain.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright. When you do stop on those stairs, what exactly do you notice, if you would not call it pain?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): If I have to be very honest, there is a tight feeling. When I climb the stairs, or if I walk fast to catch the train, the chest feels tight, like a band across it. I slow down and it eases. I would still not call that pain.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he goes quiet. He will not admit the same thing at home also.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long has this tightness been happening?

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): I was going to say from January, after the cold, but that is wrong. It is more recent, after the summer, so about three months. I kept blaming late dinner and gas, all that, and I carried on.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): And it comes only when you exert yourself? Not when you are sitting quietly?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Not when I am sitting, no. Television, the office chair, lying down, nothing happens. Only climbing stairs or walking fast.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Does that tight feeling spread anywhere, to the arm, the jaw, the back?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It stays across the front of the chest. It does not go anywhere else.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any sweating, giddiness, or a real shortness of breath along with it?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Sweating, no. Giddiness, no. I am a little more out of puff from the stairs themselves, but I would not say shortness of breath. If I stand still it settles in about two minutes.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): And the heart, does it race or thump at those times?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no palpitations. I even counted once on the platform and it was steady.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay. Tell me about your medicines. What are you taking these days?

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): For the pressure I take amlodipine. I had it in my mind as five milligrams, but no, the strip is ten milligrams, one tablet every morning after breakfast. The physician changed it some time back and I keep forgetting the new number.
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the aspirin he is supposed to take, he treats it like an optional sweet. Some days yes, some days no.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Ecosprin, seventy-five milligrams. The old doctor said take it for the heart. I do take it, but on and off. If the stomach feels heavy I skip, and some mornings I simply forget, so it is not every day.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Anything else that was written for you, even if you are not on it now?

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Atorvastatin, twenty milligrams at night, for the cholesterol. I stopped it in March. The calves were aching, so I left it on my own, and I have not restarted. There was also clopidogrel on one slip, but I never bought it and I never took even one tablet of that.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): So the statin has been off since March, and the clopidogrel was never started. Any allergy to a medicine, or to a food, anything like that?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergy, doctor. Nothing I know of. I had penicillin years ago for a tooth, no rash, no problem at all.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): And old illnesses I should know? Sugar, thyroid, any heart trouble in the past?

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Sugar is not there, the last test was normal, and thyroid no. No heart attack, no angioplasty, nothing of that sort. Only blood pressure, for eight years, and last year they said the cholesterol was high, which is why the statin was given.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His father had a heart attack, around seventy. His mother had pressure right till the end.

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, my father died of a heart attack at seventy, and my mother had high BP. I don't smoke, I never have. Alcohol only if there is a wedding, one small peg, not a habit. We live just the two of us now, the children are in Pune and Dubai.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): You are still going in to the office every day?

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, six days. The walk to the station is maybe ten minutes if I go slow. I have cut down on fried snacks after she shouted about the cholesterol, but festivals are festivals, I will not pretend I refused every laddoo.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me examine you. I will listen to the heart and the lungs, and look at the ankles. Just breathe normally.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Our neighbour had a bypass last year and he said this listening part is nothing, so I am not worried about it. Only the stethoscope is cold, that is all.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Heart sounds are normal, I do not hear a murmur, and the pulse is regular. The lungs are clear. There is no swelling at the ankles.

[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Putting this together, a tight feeling when you climb or hurry, with blood pressure for years and your father's heart attack, may be angina. I am not certain, it is only a working impression, and the tests have to tell us more.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Angina. I know that word from my father. But it goes away in two minutes, so I kept telling myself it is only gas from late dinner. If you say we should check, we will check.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): We should. I want an ECG, and bloods as well, fasting lipids, blood sugar, kidney tests, and a haemoglobin. Not because I have already decided it is the heart.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): I can take him for the ECG after this. The lab is doing walk-in samples till one o'clock.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He had tea and biscuits this morning. Can fasting still be done today?

[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Tea with a little milk and two glucose biscuits, around seven. If the fasting is spoiled I can come tomorrow morning without eating. I have done that before for the insurance papers.

[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Lipids and sugar are better fasting. Since you have eaten, we will do the ECG today, and you come tomorrow morning, nothing by mouth except water, for those bloods. The haemoglobin and the kidney tests can go in the same sample.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Tomorrow morning, empty stomach, only water. I will come by eight, before office. Should I take the morning amlodipine with water, or skip that also?

[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take the amlodipine with a sip of water, as usual. For the Ecosprin, please take seventy-five milligrams every day now, after food, not on and off. If the stomach pain becomes severe, stop it and tell me.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day, seventy-five, after food. I will keep the strip on the dining table so I actually see it. And the atorvastatin I should not restart on my own, yes?

[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do not restart the statin until we have the lipid result and we talk. If this tightness ever comes while you are resting, or if it lasts more than a few minutes and does not ease when you stop, you go to emergency. Don't wait for my clinic.
[SEG0053] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will see that he does not run for the train. He will argue, but I will be there.

[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. For now, avoid hurrying on the stairs, and if the tightness comes, stop and rest. We might arrange a treadmill test later, only if the ECG is abnormal or this tightness is still troubling you. Not today.

[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Treadmill I have seen on the clinic pamphlet. I can manage it if you say so. My knees are alright, only the left one clicks in the cold, nothing major. Sorry, I am talking too much.
[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): You are telling me what I need. Come back in one week with the reports, both of you if you can. We will sit and go through the ECG and the bloods properly.
[SEG0057] person_1 (NURSE): I will book the ECG now, and I will give you the lab slip for tomorrow morning, fasting.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): One week. If the reports come earlier as an SMS, should I still wait the full week?
[SEG0059] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, keep the one-week visit even if the message comes sooner. If you feel worse before that, don't wait for me, go to emergency, as I said.
[SEG0060] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We will come. Thank you, doctor. He needed somebody else to say it, not only me at home.

[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor, and thank you, sister. I will take the tablet properly, and I will not chase that train. Three months I brushed it aside, that was foolish, I can see it now.
[SEG0062] person_4 (DOCTOR): You came, that is the important part. ECG first, then home, and we meet next week.

spec.situation: Man or woman 50-70 who comes 'for a check-up' and only slowly admits a tight feeling in the chest when climbing stairs or walking fast; first denies chest pain, later describes the tightness. Takes a BP tablet and aspirin on and off. Doctor orders ECG and bloods.
features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

bad.reason: Dose, indication and current use supported; transcript says previously on-and-off, not simply once daily.
bad.text: Ecosprin (generic_name=aspirin, dose=75 mg, frequency=once daily after food, indication=for the heart, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Patient denied chest pain, saying the exertional symptom was tightness rather than pain.
Chest tightness is described as 'like a band across' the front of the chest.
Patient is a little more 'out of puff' on stairs, but says it settles if he stands still in about two minutes.
Aspirin/Ecosprin adherence detail: he was taking it on and off before this visit, skipping doses when his stomach feels heavy and sometimes simply forgetting.
Clopidogrel was prescribed on one slip but the patient never bought it and never took even one tablet.
High cholesterol was identified last year as the reason atorvastatin was started.
ECG was to be done today and fasting lipids/sugar deferred because he had already had tea with a little milk and two glucose biscuits at around 7 am.
Doctor advised fasting instructions for tomorrow's blood tests: nothing by mouth except water.
Doctor said lipids and blood sugar are better fasting, while haemoglobin and kidney tests can be done from the same sample.
Doctor advised to go to emergency if symptoms worsen before the one-week follow-up, not just if pain occurs at rest or lasts more than a few minutes.
Follow-up plan specified to return in one week with the reports, and both patient and wife were invited to come if possible.
